subject: Proposal: availability floor & latency carveouts + monthly credit ledger
messages:
From: Ben Harper <ben.harper@stellaris.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@stellaris.ai; ops@stellaris.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial SLA questions and credit model

Thanks Jasmine / Marissa — appreciate the proposal deck you sent. A few quick items we need clarified before we take this to procurement: 

1) You propose a 99.5% availability floor with monthly credits. Can you confirm how partial-month incidents are pro-rated (hourly or daily)?
2) The deck mentions a latency SLO for p95 at 1200ms. Is there a tiered credit if latency regressions are transient vs systemic?
3) We have a regulatory requirement to exclude scheduled maintenance windows agreed 30 days in advance — will those be carved out of uptime calculations?

We'd also like visibility into the monthly credit ledger so we can reconcile invoices against incidents. Can you attach a worked example?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Harper
Head of Platform Ops, Stellaris AI
ben.harper@stellaris.ai

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Ben Harper <ben.harper@stellaris.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:38:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial SLA questions and credit model

Ben — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline, and I've attached a sample ledger (SLA_credit_ledger_v3.xlsx) showing two incident scenarios. Longer notes below.

1) Partial-month proration: we calculate credits on a per-minute basis for uptime buckets; the ledger uses minutes to compute the % and the resulting credit for the month. That keeps reconciliation exact for short incidents.

2) Latency SLOs: we propose a two-tier latency remedy: a small fixed credit band for transient p95 spikes (<3 discrete spikes in a 30d window) and a proportional credit for sustained regressions (p95 above threshold for >24 continuous hours). This is because transient spikes are often noisy and not necessarily platform defects. We can make thresholds more conservative if Stellaris prefers.

3) Scheduled maintenance: yes — scheduled maintenance windows agreed in writing 30+ days in advance are carved out. We keep a public maintenance calendar and include agreed windows in the monthly reconciliation.

Action items I propose:
- I'll send the filled ledger for your baseline month (using May traffic) so we can validate numbers (attached).
- Marissa/Legal to confirm whether the two-tier latency language is acceptable or if you want a single proportional remedy.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Account Lead — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0124

Attachment: SLA_credit_ledger_v3.xlsx (worksheet: worked examples)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Initial SLA questions and credit model

Ben — adding a little more color from the operations/financial perspective and a proposed compact clause that could appear in the SOW: 

Proposed compact SLA clause (draft):
- Availability: Redwood will target a monthly uptime of 99.5% measured to the minute. Monthly credits will be issued on a prorated per-minute basis for the portion of time below the threshold.
- Latency: For p95 latency > 1200ms, Redwood will apply a tiered remedy:
  * Tier A (transient): if the p95 breach resolves within 24 hours and occurs fewer than 3 times in the billing month -> one-time credit equal to 2% of that month's Redwood service fees.
  * Tier B (sustained): if p95 is above threshold for >24 continuous hours -> proportional credit equal to the percentage delta below the uptime target applied to the monthly fee (worked example in ledger).
- Scheduled maintenance: Windows agreed 30+ days in advance and posted on the maintenance calendar are excluded. Emergencies where Redwood requests an expedited maintenance window must be notified 72 hours prior where possible; otherwise, they are considered part of uptime unless mutually agreed.

We prefer per-minute proration to avoid disputes and to make the ledger straightforward for invoice reconciliation. We've attached the ledger and a redline-ready SOW paragraph (redwood-sla-proposal-aug2026.pdf).

Please let us know if procurement needs different wording on remedies (fixed cap per month, maximum aggregate credit, etc.).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success & Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-sla-proposal-aug2026.pdf

Thanks Marissa/Jasmine — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement after reviewing the draft: 

• Cap: Procurement prefers a monthly cap expressed as a dollar amount rather than a percentage of monthly spend (they find it easier for budgeting). Can you suggest a recommended cap tier (e.g., $10k / $25k / $50k) tied to commitment level?
• Latency transient threshold: they'd like the transient definition tightened to <2 discrete spikes per 30d window (instead of 3).
• Ledger access: can you provide a read-only sheet we can query each month (a link) versus attached XLSX?

Next steps: If you can propose a three-tier cap mapping and update the transient threshold to 2 spikes, we can take this to legal next week. Also would appreciate a public link for monthly ledger reconciliation.

I'll loop in our procurement lead once you've had a chance to respond.

Best,
Ben
